title: hello-workflow — a deterministic two-step pipeline (target: workflow)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A two-step sequential agent: step 1 lists the directory, step 2 summarizes what it found.” Note what the “Run it” block does *not* offer: no `crewhaus run`. A workflow ships as a bundle you boot yourself — Beat 3 shows you why.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: two steps, in order

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Three lines: what it's called, which runtime spine to compile, which model runs the steps.”

beats.label: Write down the trap
beats.cue: “Workflow steps run single-turn — there's no interactive surface to prompt on.”

beats.label: Allow Bash explicitly
beats.cue: Anything that would ask becomes deny — so grant Bash here, or step 1 never runs ls -la.

beats.label: Step 1 · list-files
beats.cue: “Run ls -la. Report in 1–3 short sentences. Do not editorialize beyond what the listing shows.”

beats.label: Fence step 1's tools
beats.cue: Tools are granted per step, not per agent — step 1 gets bash, and nothing else.

beats.label: Step 2 · summarize
beats.cue: “You will receive the previous step's directory listing as context.” — and it calls no tools.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Two steps, each with its own instructions, model and tool grant — that's the whole program.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target workflow (2 steps)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted pipeline
beats.cue: “Step 1's answer is seeded into step 2 as ‘## Output of previous step’ — the thread is code.”

beats.label: Try to ship it to the edge
beats.cue: “Refused: step 1 runs a host shell, and a Cloudflare Worker has no shell to run it in.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — cf-worker cannot run the host tool `bash`; the compiler refuses instead of dropping it

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL — a workflow isn't a chat.” It doesn't just fail: it names the shapes it does take. That's the reason the README's “Run it” block boots the bundle instead.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "workflow")`. The starter README documents the compile --check → `bun dist/agent.ts` path instead, and says in as many words that run is cli/browser-only.

beats.label: Boot the compiled pipeline
beats.cue: [needs-key] “So you boot the bundle: step 1/2 looks around, step 2/2 summarizes, and it exits.”

verify.note: runs both steps against Anthropic; deps were installed by the --check beat

beats.label: Start the store empty
beats.cue: The run id is fixed, so take two would replay take one. Clear the store and the contrast is real.

verify.note: re-take hygiene: `take-1` is a stable id, so without this the very first boot below would return take one's cached steps instead of running them, and the two beats would look identical

beats.label: Name the run, store the steps
beats.cue: [needs-key] A stable run id plus a file store: every finished step is recorded as it completes.

verify.note: same two steps; records land under live/idem/hello-workflow — inside the gitignored scratch dir, so a take leaves no diff (the bare `file` value would write .crewhaus/idempotency/, which is NOT ignored)

beats.label: Boot the same run again
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Resumes at the first not-yet-completed step” — the finished ones never re-run.

verify.note: durable exactly-once replay: completed steps return their cached result instead of re-running; same run id and same store as the beat above
